headline: No 64–68 break anywhere; Wednesday the softer bluefin look
body:
Fog is the safety item, not wind: patchy dense fog with visibility 1 NM or less offshore both mornings, so run radar and sound signals outbound. The east channel stays easy — 2 to 3 ft, NW 5–10 going W 10–15 this afternoon, and lighter again Wednesday. The triangle sits at 3.5 ft today with 13 kn gusting 15 at dawn, easing to 3.4 ft and near calm at first light Wednesday. West of there it's rough: Santa Rosa Flats holds 15–20 kn WNW and 4.5 ft both days, San Nicolas 4.5 ft, Osborn 4.1–4.3 ft.

The honest call is that neither day is a bluefin day on temperature. Nothing in the data touches the 64–68 band — the triangle corners read 71.2 west, 72.8 south and 73.0 east today, 71.2/73.1/73.6 Wednesday, and the outer grounds are warmer still at 71.0 to 73.4. The break has not slid to another ground; it simply isn't on this chart. If you go, take Wednesday's calm morning and work the west corner's 71.2 edge, the only cool water showing. The long runs aren't worth the fuel.
